Nlaka'pamux

Nlaka’pamux connects distinct communities and representative organizations. This path introduces the Nation Tribal Council’s language and cultural-care work, a dated personal reflection, and the particular Lytton First Nation–BC Parks planning history of Stein Valley.

01

Identity and context

Nlaka’pamux is a people’s name also encountered under the historical outside name Thompson.

Read the sources [1] www2.gov.bc.ca

02

A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Language, Fraser and Thompson river homelands and community-specific institutions. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] www2.gov.bc.ca [2] Province of British Columbia [3] BC Parks / Stein Valley Nlaka’pamux Heritage Park Management Board

03

Different communities and institutional voices

The provincial listing distinguishes communities and representative organizations. The Tribal Council’s Cultural Resources account describes its own work in language and education. These sources should not be collapsed into a claim that a single organization speaks for every Nlaka’pamux person.

Read the sources [2] Province of British Columbia [4] Nlaka’pamux Nation Tribal Council

04

A particular cooperative-management history

The 2000 Stein Valley plan describes a process involving BC Parks, Lytton First Nation and a shared Management Board. It recounts advocacy and the 1995 park designation. The selected planning history offers a concrete institutional example; its agreements and present management arrangements need separate review.

Read the sources [3] BC Parks / Stein Valley Nlaka’pamux Heritage Park Management Board

05

A dated reflection on apology and action

In the Council’s 2022 newsletter, Matt Pasco reflects on his Vatican trip and argues that apology must be accompanied by meaningful action. He also questions approaches that treat distinct Indigenous peoples as one undifferentiated group. This is an attributed personal and political account, not a universal community response.

Read the sources [5] Nlaka’pamux Nation Tribal Council; Chief Matt Pasco, as identified in 2022

What needs further research

  • Read original park agreements and selected public historical records without exposing protected cultural places.

Stein Valley Nlaka’pamux Heritage Park Management Plan, June 2000 — selected planning history ↗

Publication: 2000-06

A jointly coordinated planning process describes Lytton First Nation participation and the park’s preservation history. This particular partnership does not represent all Nlaka’pamux communities.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual PDF p.8 acknowledgments and pp.11–14 / printed1–4:plan highlights, process, cooperative management and 1995 designation background.74 pages obtained; no whole-file reading claimed.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal HTTP200 PDF/text read. Prepared by BC Parks with consultants, coordinated through the Management Board and informed by Elders. Original agreements, laws, maps, site records, ceremonial practices and current visitor rules uninspected.

Cultural Resources — language, education and cultural stewardship account ↗

The Council connects language, education and cultural stewardship, crediting the people who developed language resources. Read as its institutional account rather than every community’s experience.

Chair’s Reflections from the Vatican Trip — NNTC newsletter, July–September 2022 ↗

Publication: 2022-07/2022-09

A dated personal reflection distinguishes apology from material action and questions treating distinct Indigenous peoples as interchangeable. It is Pasco’s stated interpretation, not a unanimous response.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual complete Chair’s Reflections on PDF/printed pp.2–3; cover title, issue period and byline also read.12-page issue obtained, not fully read.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal HTTP200 PDF/text read after slow retrieval; web reader rejected14MB size. No underlying testimony, Church record or other newsletter article inspected. Personal/family details and ceremonial descriptions are not reproduced.
